desc: A collier's kilns under their turf, turning wood into charcoal whenever wood can be had: the fuel that burns hottest. vq6n1z
name: Charcoal burner

desc: Whenever game can be had, it sends out hunting parties over the surrounding country and brings back venison, pelts, and game to sell. It doubles as the local authority on the wilds, the safe trails and the treacherous ones. vq6n2z
name: Hunter's lodge

desc: Requires a market charter. A principal source of the town's trade. vq6n3z
name: Weekly market

desc: The central plaza where the weekly market and the fairs are held. vq6n4z
name: Market square

desc: Regional merchants. Luxury goods available. vq6n5z
name: Annual fair

desc: Control trade in specific goods. vq6n6z
name: Merchant guilds (3-8)

desc: Lodging for traveling merchants. vq6n7z
name: Inn (multiple)

desc: Drinking houses, and the town's gathering places. vq6n8z
name: Taverns (5-20)

desc: Grain kept in common, a hedge against lean harvests and hunger. vq6n9z
name: Town granary

desc: A licensed house that pays for road news and keeps the register: who arrived, from where, and what they carried word of. Cheap to run and openly taxed, and found wherever the roads bring traffic. vq6n10z
name: Listening post

desc: Grain ground at several sites. vq6n11z
name: Mills (2-5)

desc: Multiple craftsmen organized under a guild. Standard arrows by the sheaf, specialty broadheads, composite bows to commission. Restocks merchant caravans and outfits their guards. vq6n12z
name: Bowyers & fletchers (guild)

desc: Cloth-work, more often than not guild-run. vq6n13z
name: Weavers/Textile workers

desc: Master clothiers cutting garments from finished cloth, working clothes and household livery alike. vq6n14z
name: Tailor's guild

desc: The butchering trade, strictly overseen. vq6n15z
name: Butchers (3-8)

desc: Converts raw ore to refined metal using charcoal-fueled furnaces, whenever ore can be had. vq6n16z
name: Smelter

desc: Rope and cordage twisted from hemp, flax, or whatever plant fibre comes to hand. Nothing sails, rises, or is harvested without it. vq6n17z
name: Ropemaker

desc: Regulate quality, prices, and apprenticeships. vq6n18z
name: Craft guilds (5-15)

desc: Several houses of worship within town. vq6n19z
name: Parish churches (2-5)

desc: Each congregation buries its own, and the sexton keeps the roll that inheritance disputes are settled from. Guilds buy plots together so their members lie among their trade. vq6n20z
name: Parish burial grounds

desc: A council of prominent citizens sees to the town's common affairs. Less accountable than an elected council, but steady. vq6n21z
name: Town council

desc: Buildings of several storeys, in timber and stone. vq6n22z
name: Housing (75-650 households)

desc: Wells and fountains, or water carried in by pipe. vq6n23z
name: Multiple water sources

desc: Meeting place and administrative center. vq6n24z
name: Town hall

desc: Part-time guards. Night patrol and gate duty. vq6n25z
name: Town watch

desc: Trade in forbidden goods, kept off the tax rolls. vq6n26z
name: Smuggling operation

desc: Gated stone defences. Costly to raise and no cheaper to keep up. vq6n27z
name: Town walls

desc: Full-scale tannery with multiple vats and a guild-trained workforce. Produces high-quality leather for shoes, armour, and saddlery. vq6n28z
name: Tanner (established)

desc: Bread production. Guild-regulated prices. vq6n29z
name: Bakers (5-15)
